source_evidence: Carefully read all of the fund’s available information, including its registration statement, prospectus, and any recent 10-Ks, 10-Qs, and 8-Ks.
question: Misconception: A brief description of a publicly traded BDC is enough to understand it, so there’s no need to review its filings or ask questions.
answer: Correction: BDCs can be complex and have unique risks. Before investing, review the fund’s available information, including its registration statement, prospectus, and recent reports. Also examine its fees, strategy, investments, risks, debt, and distribution history.
